We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH (anilide with an extra NH on phenyl? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amino group para? Wait Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amino at position 1 and 6? Actually SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with two amino groups ortho? It's an aniline with amino at both ends? It's a phenyl with NH at position 1 and NH at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the ring has an NH attached at position 1 (the N before c3) and also an NH attached at the last N after the ring (attached to the same carbon? That seems like a diamino phenyl (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide attaches to an aniline that also has an NH group (para to amide). So final product has sulfonamide linking p-tolyl to phenyl, and that phenyl has trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). So we need 3 steps retrosynthesis.

Given hints: step 1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So we can disconnect the amide bond between the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl and the aniline (Nc3...). So precursor: the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (trans-CH=CH-COOH attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl) and the aniline (p-phenylenediamine). So step 1: amide coupling.

Step 2: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So disconnect the double bond: the aldehyde precursor is the aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl sulfonyl phenyl with aldehyde at para position? Actually the double bond is attached to phenyl ring via CH=CH-CO... The α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring at the position where the double bond is conjugated. So the aldehyde would be the same phenyl ring bearing a formyl group (CHO) attached to the sulfonyl phenyl. So step 2: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (Doebner). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl-CHO) and malonic acid (or its derivative). But we can consider malonic acid as simple reagent.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: connect p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride with the aromatic amine (the phenyl ring that will later become aldehyde). So disconnect the sulfonamide bond: we need p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and the aniline (the phenyl ring that will later be functionalized). So the aromatic amine is the phenyl that later gets aldehyde (via formylation). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (which is the phenyl ring). So overall 3 steps.

Thus retrosynthesis tree: target molecule (root). Reaction 1 (amide coupling) with template for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Children: precursor A (α,β-unsaturated acid) and precursor B (p-phenylenediamine). Reaction 2 (Doebner) on precursor A: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. Children: aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (simple). Reaction 3 (sulfonamide formation) on aldehyde precursor: sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide aldehyde. Children: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (which is the same phenyl ring). The aniline also is the same as the aromatic amine used later for amide coupling? Actually the aniline is the phenyl that later becomes aldehyde and also later is used as amine for amide coupling (p-phenylenediamine). Wait we have two amine functionalities on that phenyl: one is the sulfonamide nitrogen (attached to sulfonyl) and the other is the free amine (para to sulfonamide) that will be used for amide coupling. In our target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl sulfonyl group, and the other amine is attached to the amide carbonyl (via NH-CO). So the phenyl ring has two substituents: sulfonamide at one position (connected to p-tolyl sulfonyl) and amide at another position (connected via CH=CH-CO-NH-). The amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (aniline) which also has an NH2 group (the same as the amide nitrogen? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the aniline). The phenyl also has an NH2 group at the other para position (the free amine). So the aniline used for amide coupling is the same phenyl that also undergoes sulfonamide formation at a different position. So in retrosynthesis, we can treat the aromatic amine (p-phenylenediamine) as the starting material that already has two amine groups. One amine will be sulfonylated (step 3) to give sulfonamide aldehyde; the other amine remains free for later amide coupling (step 1). So we don't need separate aniline precursor; we can use p-phenylenediamine as the core.

Thus step 3: sulfonyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine -> sulfonamide aldehyde (where one amine is sulfonylated, the other remains free). The aldehyde is introduced later via formylation? Wait the aldehyde is on the phenyl ring after sulfonamide formation. The aldehyde is at the position para to sulfonamide? In target, the aldehyde is not present; it's part of the unsaturated acid after Doebner. The aldehyde is the precursor to the unsaturated acid. So after sulfonamide formation, we have a phenyl ring with sulfonamide at one position and an aldehyde at another (para). So step 2 will convert aldehyde to unsaturated acid (Doebner). So that works.
